scope_note: SG-MA-PHARMACIST-ADMINISTRATION after corrections following the V10C audit. The section no longer treats the Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 eligible-medication list as the whole of the administration authority: a new table and the prose now state what 105 CMR 700.004(B)(6) (immunization by a registered pharmacist, pharmacy intern or pharmacy technician on a practitioner's order, for influenza, COVID-19 and Department-designated immunizations of patients aged 5 or older, under conditions (a)-(d)), 700.004(B)(9)(e) and 700.003(F) each authorise, pointing to SG-MA-PUBLIC-HEALTH-STANDING-ORDERS for 700.003(F); retrieval_prompts[30] and quick_review[8] are limited to the circular's pathway. orientation[10] now explains why the broad reading cannot stand instead of offering one safe course for both readings; a methadone document is no longer called valid, and a federal note on 21 CFR 1306.07(a) and (d) rests on FED-NARCOTIC-MAINTENANCE-DETOX-ROUTES; single-dose prescribing is a condition on the pharmacist or intern rather than a prescriber duty; orientation[4] shows which text names the intern. New rule: MA-PHARMACY-IMMUNIZATION-ADMINISTRATION; MA-EMERGENCY-VACCINE-GATE is now cited. The published SG-MA-PHARMACY-TECHNICIANS teaches the 247 CMR 8.00 limits on technicians and does not mention 700.004(B)(6); that is recorded for a later repair of that section. MA-Q-0329 left the practice links because its stem calls a methadone prescription for addiction treatment valid. Scope gate: all 11 actionable signals declined; they are collaborative drug therapy management prescribing records (MA-CDTM-*), MA-PHARMACIST-PRESCRIBER-ID and MA-HORMONAL-CONTRACEPTIVE, which concern prescribing rather than administration.

prior_audit_reference.note: V10C rated the superseded hash MINOR_EDIT and drove this correction. It does not bind the hash frozen here and is excluded from the auditor package.
